_why: WHAT A TURN COST, AS ONE CORPUS EVERY PLANE READS (#727).
#300 added per-turn usage to the fastapi and django planes in the same shape, and gave
each its own expectations. The node plane got neither: `apps/node-backend` had ZERO
occurrences of `usage` or `token`, so every layer above the model on that runtime said a
turn cost nothing -- which is the exact misreport #232 opened and #300 was meant to end.
NOTHING COULD HAVE NOTICED. check-run-axes-parity holds the two PYTHON planes
byte-identical and correctly excludes node -- 'identical' has no meaning across languages,
and apps/node-backend/README.md says so. What covers node for run axes is
run-axes-cases.json: one corpus, read by all three planes, so a case added there is added
everywhere at once. That mechanism existed and had never been pointed at usage.
This is that corpus for usage. It is the reason a divergence on one plane is now a RED on
that plane rather than a silence.
EVERY CASE IS PLANE-INDEPENDENT ON PURPOSE. The inputs are `usage_metadata` objects in
the shape LangChain exposes on both runtimes -- `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` /
`total_tokens`, verified snake_case in @langchain/core 1.2.9 and in the Python planes --
so the same expectation holds on all three and a case cannot quietly become a per-plane
assertion.
WHAT THIS FIXTURE IS NOT ABOUT. It states the VALUE a turn reports, not where that value
rides on the wire. The wire location is #714's subject (`messageMetadata.totalUsage`, not
a top-level `totalUsage`, which AI SDK v6 rejects outright) and is guarded by
packages/test-utils/src/finish-frame-conformance.test.ts and
scripts/sse_frame_conformance.py. Keeping the two apart means a change to either can be
landed and reverted without dragging the other.
_mustContainWhy: A reader must assert these three ids are present, so that a case cannot be quietly
dropped from the corpus and leave the reader green over a smaller question.
These three because each is a DIFFERENT failure. `several-calls-summed` fails if a plane
overwrites instead of summing -- wrong in the direction that looks plausible, since a
smaller number nobody questions. `nothing-reported` fails if a plane emits a zeroed block,
which asserts the turn was free on no evidence. `zeros-are-not-a-report` fails if a plane
treats an explicit zero differently from silence; the two are indistinguishable downstream

cases.why: The base case. One model call reporting usage; the turn's cost is that call's.

A TURN IS NOT ONE MODEL CALL. plan-execute makes several. Overwriting instead of summing reports the last call's cost as the turn's -- wrong in the direction that looks plausible, because a smaller number is one nobody questions.

Most chunks in a stream carry no usage at all -- it arrives on the last chunk of each model call. A plane that resets on a silent chunk, or that counts one as a zero-usage call, gets a different answer than one that skips it.

A provider may report some fields and not others. The absent ones count as zero rather than making the whole report absent -- half a measurement is still a measurement, and dropping it would lose the half that was real.

A TURN THAT BOUGHT INPUT AND PRODUCED NO OUTPUT STILL COST SOMETHING (#734). The emit condition read `totalTokens or outputTokens` and never consulted `inputTokens`, which was accumulated and read by nothing -- so 100 tokens of context reported as a free turn. This case differs from `zeros-are-not-a-report` in exactly ONE field, which is the point: the pair separates "report a turn the provider measured" from "always report", and a repair that satisfies this case by emitting unconditionally breaks that one.

A provider that reports ONLY a total has still reported. This case exists because mutation testing showed the `totalTokens` term in the emit predicate was undiscriminated by every other case -- `single-call` and the rest all carry a non-zero output, so dropping `totalTokens` from the condition changed no verdict. That was true before #734 as well; the term was carried and never tested. A predicate term no case can distinguish is a term nobody can tell has stopped working.

THE HALF THAT KEEPS THE NUMBER HONEST. Emitting a zeroed usage block asserts the turn was free -- a claim the backend has no basis for and one that is indistinguishable downstream from a real zero. Absence must stay absent.

A provider that answers with explicit zeros has told us nothing a provider that stayed silent did not. The two are indistinguishable downstream, so they must be indistinguishable here -- and a plane that emitted a zeroed block for this one would be making the claim `nothing-reported` exists to prevent, by a different route.
